answer: Cross-Epoch Trajectory Matching. Each identity commits a random hidden point (vertex) per epoch; later epochs must reveal a path consistent with prior movement under a fixed drift bound. An attacker running N clones must fund N independent trajectories, since shared paths collapse to one identity at the glacier checkpoint. Inconsistent histories forfeit a per-identity continuity deposit harvested across the grove of verified peers, so each clone costs a full fresh history plus deposit, scaling linearly with N.
